title: fix: preserve surrogate pairs in shared and command truncation
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14562

Part of #14562 (shared string helpers and command-output paths; remaining paths listed below).

### Description

Add a dependency-free `sliceUtf16` helper that moves slice boundaries inward when they would split a UTF-16 surrogate pair. Use it in `truncateStr`, both `truncateSplit` paths, and `truncateCommandOutput`. Keep existing UTF-16 budgets, head/tail proportions, recovery notices, and streamed total counts. No breaking changes or grapheme-cluster guarantee; existing malformed input is not repaired.

The helper is exported from both shared entry points so core can reuse the node export while browser consumers retain the same shared string API.

This is intentionally the small shared-helper/command-output portion of the issue, not a claim that all reported implementations are fixed. Follow-ups remain in message-builder (including byte backstop), search, file-read, compaction, budget projection, and hook context truncation.

title: feat(core): flag-gated computer-use section in the cloud session prompt
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A. This is part of the computer-use rollout for cloud sessions ("closing the loop"). Related: #15393 (artifact attach/render), core-platform #3577 (artifact endpoints), core-platform #3581 (sandbox learns its session ID).

### Description

This lets cloud-session agents check their own UI changes. Behind a new `cloud-computer-use` feature flag, the cloud session's system prompt gets a section that tells the agent how to:

- start a virtual display (Xvfb) in the sandbox,
- launch the app in Chromium,
- drive it with xdotool,
- take screenshots with ImageMagick,
- look at the screenshots with `read_files`,
- publish the frames that prove the change with `publish-artifacts --files <list.json> --attach`, so they appear in the user's chat.

This is the "main agent drives it directly" v1 we agreed on. Moving the work into a computer-use subagent and adding a `present` tool for captioned slideshows come later.

**Where it hooks in.** All clients create cloud tasks through the hub daemon's `CloudSessionController`. It builds the system prompt in `buildCloudSessionSystemPrompt` and sends it with `session.create`. Note that on the sandbox hub this prompt *replaces* the normal Cline prompt (`resolveBootstrapSystemPrompt` returns `config.systemPrompt` verbatim). So the new section is written to stand on its own instead of assuming the base prompt's tool guidance.

**Gating.** The section is added only when both of these hold:

1. **The model can see images.** It must be in the bundled `cline` catalog with the `images` capability. Models missing from the catalog are treated as text-only. This is deliberately stricter than `modelSupportsImageInput({})`, which assumes support when capabilities are unknown, so the section never reaches a model whose `read_files` would reject screenshots. The check runs first and is cheap, so non-vision models never hit the flag service.
2. **The flag is on.** This is `isClineAccountFeatureEnabled(FeatureFlag.CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE)`, the same account-scoped PostHog check Composio uses inside the hub daemon, where the client's in-memory flag service isn't available. It's cached for 60s and fails closed. For local development, `CLINE_CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE=1` in the environment the hub daemon inherits turns it on without PostHog.

The controller takes the gate as an injected `isComputerUseEnabled` option. That keeps the controller free of flag and env lookups and makes it easy to test. If the gate throws, the section is left out.

The section is added to both the new-task prompt and the local-to-cloud handoff prompt. It only affects new tasks: existing tasks keep the prompt they were created with.

**Prompt content.** It's adapted from the computer-use spec, with these changes:

- `chromium` instead of `google-chrome`, because the base image is Debian (`node:24-slim`), and window search by `--class chromium`.
- `--no-sandbox` added to the Chromium flags. Chromium's own sandbox doesn't work as a non-root user in this container.
- A tools check first (`command -v Xvfb xdotool import chromium`), with "skip, don't install" if anything is missing. The sandbox runs as `node` without sudo, and the tools arrive via the base image.
- The evidence-file folder (`/tmp/cu-shots/evidence/*.json`) is replaced with `publish-artifacts --attach`, which already exists on cloud-platform's `feat/session-artifacts` branch. The agent describes each published screenshot in its answer, since loose images have no captions yet.

### Test Procedure

- New controller tests:
  - The section is added when the flag is on and the model takes images.
  - It's left out when the flag is off.
  - It's left out when the model isn't in the catalog.
  - It's left out when the gate throws.
- `vitest run src/cloud/controller.test.ts`: 112 passed. `src/hub/server/cloud-session-service.test.ts`: 56 passed.
- `bun run typecheck` in core (dev + smoke) and `tsc` in shared are clean.
- I checked that the new `@cline/llms` import in `cloud/` doesn't reach the desktop webview: its `@cline/core/cloud` imports are type-only.

**Not yet tested end to end.** That needs pieces that haven't merged or deployed:

- core-platform #3581, so the sandbox gets `CLINE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`.
- cloud-platform `feat/session-artifacts`, which ships the `publish-artifacts` command, after #15393 merges and the SDK is released.
- The computer-use tools in the base image (Marlon).

Until those land, a flagged agent will find the tools missing and skip verification, as the prompt tells it to.

To try it once they land: run desktop with `CLINE_CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE=1`, start a cloud task on a vision model in a repo with a web UI, and ask for a visible change. Published screenshots should appear in the chat.

### Type of Change

-   [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`)
-   [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Additional Notes

- The `cloud-computer-use` flag still needs to be created in PostHog. Until then everyone evaluates to off, except dev builds using the env override.
- The first flagged task per minute waits on one PostHog poll before `session.create`. The cache and fail-closed behavior bound this.
- Follow-ups: a `present` tool with title, captions and pass/fail (replacing loose images); a computer-use subagent to keep screenshots out of the main context; artifact rendering outside desktop.

title: feat: link to web app privacy settings from account views
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** no GitHub issue; Linear DAT-111. This is a smaller alternative to #15043 that covers just the privacy settings link.

The diff is 224 added lines across 16 files, compared with 1,381 across 46 in #15043. The other parts of #15043 (the desktop sign-out race fix, `client=` attribution, and environment-aware links across the desktop app) can follow as separate PRs if they're wanted.

### Description

`GET /users/me` now returns `dataPrivacyPath` (for example `/dashboard/account?tab=privacy`), the Cline web app page where users manage Restrict Data Use and Cline Bench preferences. Each client shows a **Privacy settings** link only when the field is present, so older or self-hosted backends show nothing new.

- **`@cline/shared`:** `resolveClineAppUrl(path, appBaseUrl)`, next to `getClineEnvironmentConfig`. It resolves a path against the web app and returns `undefined` if either input is missing or the result would leave the app's origin (another host, protocol-relative, `javascript:`, plain `http`). The path comes from the server, so this keeps a bad value from becoming a link to somewhere else.
- **`@cline/core`:** `ClineAccountUser.dataPrivacyPath?: string`.
- **CLI:** the account snapshot builds `privacySettingsUrl` on the environment's `appBaseUrl`, and `/account` adds a **Privacy settings** action that opens it in the browser and leaves the dialog open.
- **VS Code and JetBrains:** `data_privacy_path` is added to the `UserInfo` proto and passed through `AuthService.getInfo()`. The Account view adds a **Privacy settings** button under Dashboard / Log out, using the same `appBaseUrl` as the Dashboard button. `ClineAuthContext` now replaces the user when any field changes, not only `uid`. Token refreshes re-fetch `/users/me` for the same user, so without this the new field would never reach the webview.
- **Desktop:** the Account view adds a shield **Privacy settings** button next to **Open dashboard**.

Deliberately not in this PR:
- No `client=` attribution parameter, since the dashboard doesn't read it yet.
- Existing dashboard links aren't migrated or hidden. Desktop links stay as they are, including those hardcoded to production, and the new desktop link uses `getClineEnvironmentConfig().appBaseUrl` like `welcome-chat.tsx`. Making every desktop account link follow the environment is a separate change.
- No handling for a provider `baseUrl` override when picking the web app.

### Screenshots

Not captured. The new controls only render for a signed-in account whose `/users/me` includes `dataPrivacyPath`. The controls match the ones in the #15043 screenshots.

**Issue:** Related to #15379.

The CLI rebuilds models discovered from OpenAI-compatible endpoints using only IDs and names. This drops runtime `knownModels` metadata, so known reasoning models skip the effort picker and disable reasoning when selected.

title: fix(llms): give adaptive-thinking Claude requests the full output budget
body:
## Problem

Adaptive thinking (Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5) counts inside `max_tokens`. When no `maxTokens` is set, the gateway sends `max(32000, 0.3 × model.maxOutputTokens)` — **38,400** for these models. At `--thinking high` the models often think 20–70k tokens on one step, so the call is cut off mid-thought:

- the response has no answer text (finish reason: length), and the thinking is billed and discarded
- the agent then retries with the "output-token limit reached" nudge

In a DeepSWE benchmark campaign (Oct 20, OpenRouter, `--thinking high`), this showed up as ~6-minute calls with 0 output followed by the nudge.

## Fix

For adaptive-thinking requests (`isAdaptiveThinkingRequest`: Claude adaptive-era model id + reasoning enabled), the synthesized default uses the model's **full** advertised output budget (128k) instead of 30% of it.

- still clamped by the context window
- an explicit `maxTokens` still wins
- non-adaptive and non-Claude models are unchanged

## Testing

- New tests in `gateway.test.ts` (128k default, context clamp, explicit override) and `model-facts.test.ts`
- Wire capture: Opus/Sonnet 5.5 now send `max_tokens: 128000`; other models unchanged
- Reran 4 tasks × Opus/Sonnet × 3 on Prime with a 3.0.73 build containing this patch: **0 output-limit truncations** (previously frequent). Calls with 46–77k thinking tokens now complete instead of being cut off.

## Notes for reviewers

- This removes truncation; it does **not** make runs faster. At high effort calls that used to be cut off at ~6 min now finish (some take up to ~12 min). The slowness comes from `high` effort itself and is a separate default question.
- OpenRouter may reserve credit against `max_tokens`; a 128k request could hit "insufficient credits" for low-balance keys. Worth a sanity check.

The [old desktop code](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/16bade5c13bca13c58a25770ad6a0d40c4f1482d/apps/examples/desktop-app/sidecar/cloud-sessions.ts#L223-L234) used the environment API root; the [new Hub code](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/5a5e5acb7dc6163d7f59b16d890e60c764e47318/sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/cloud-session-service.ts#L226-L231) prefers the saved Cline inference URL. When that URL ends in `/api/v1`, the cloud client [concatenates the base and path](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/7266ccc9f1476e67265a8f0f8c08d6ed5f3b1e7a/sdk/packages/core/src/cloud/api.ts#L337), producing `/api/v1/api/v1/session`. The resulting 404 can make session discovery return an empty list.

Strip the trailing version suffix when constructing the Hub's cloud dependencies. Preserve the saved host, any preceding REST path prefix, and the environment fallback. Keeping the saved host also keeps cloud requests aligned with authentication. The stored inference setting is unchanged.

Validation: 113 focused tests pass. A local HTTP integration test with synthetic credentials exercises token refresh, account lookup, and session discovery against the same saved backend, including when the environment points elsewhere. Tests cover root/versioned URLs, trailing slashes, a REST path prefix, and the environment fallback. Full build/typecheck remain blocked locally by workspace dependency gaps; CI is still required.

Longer term, consolidate Cline API-root resolution after verifying each caller’s URL contract, including custom hosts and path prefixes. Related code:

- [CLI free-model lookup](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/7266ccc9f1476e67265a8f0f8c08d6ed5f3b1e7a/apps/cli/src/utils/free-model-cost.ts#L22-L27) already removes a terminal `/api/v1` before constructing the endpoint.

- [Desktop connector base resolution](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/7266ccc9f1476e67265a8f0f8c08d6ed5f3b1e7a/apps/examples/desktop-app/sidecar/cline-auth.ts#L87-L94) trims trailing slashes only, then [appends the connector API path](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/7266ccc9f1476e67265a8f0f8c08d6ed5f3b1e7a/apps/examples/desktop-app/sidecar/cline-connectors-api.ts#L112).

title: fix: pass commit search terms to git as arguments, not shell text
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15377

### Description

Commit search hands the typed query to a shell command, so the shell eats the quotes before `git log` sees them.

`apps/vscode/src/utils/git.ts` interpolated the query into a command string:

```ts
const { stdout } = await execAsync(
	`git log -n 10 --format="..." --date=short ` + `--grep="${query}" --regexp-ignore-case`,
	{ cwd },
)
```

With `"quoted"` as the query, `git` receives `--grep=quoted`, so it also returns commits that only contain the unquoted word. The same pattern was used for the hash fallback (`--author-date-order ${query}`) and for `getCommitInfo()`, where the revision comes from a mention (`@<hash>`) and was also spliced into the command string.

The file already solves this exact problem for file names, and says so:

```ts
// Pass the filename as a separate argv entry (no shell) so names containing
// quotes, `$`, backticks, or spaces can't be interpreted as shell syntax.
```

This PR applies that same pattern to the five remaining call sites: the query and the revision are now single `argv` entries via `execFileAsync("git", [...])`.

The resulting summed input count is also used as if it were the size of one prompt, which can trigger premature context compaction.

title: fix(hub): stop re-sending a rejected Cline refresh token on every cloud poll
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** none filed. Found during a post-release telemetry check of core 0.2.0 (shipped with desktop 0.0.49).

### Description

#### What telemetry showed

In the first 3 hours after the Oct 26 release, the hub (`cline-hub-daemon`) on core 0.2.0 logged:

- **32,805 `user.auth_logged_out` events from 49 machines.** Core 0.0.95 logged 46 in the same window. That works out to ~670 per affected machine, or about one every 16 seconds.
- **~52,000 `user.auth_refresh_soft_failure` events (`errorName: OAuthReauthRequiredError`) from 94 users.** That's 85% of all hub error events.
- **Hub errors per task: 13.3, against a 1.4–1.9 baseline.**

The interval matched the cloud session controller's poll cadence (~12s median between events per machine). The affected users were all signed out server-side: their stored refresh token had been revoked or had expired.

#### Cause

`HubCloudSessionService` was added in #15205. Its `createController` passes a `getAuthToken` closure to `CloudSessionController`, `CloudSessionApi` and `ClineAccountService`, and the controller calls it on every poll. Each call goes through `RuntimeOAuthTokenManager.resolveProviderApiKey`, which refreshes when the access token has expired.

For a user whose refresh token the auth server rejects, each poll went through these steps:

1. `resolveProviderApiKey` sends the dead refresh token to the auth server.
2. The server rejects it. The refresh path emits `user.auth_logged_out` and throws `OAuthReauthRequiredError`.
3. `getAuthToken` correctly skips the stored-key fallback, but `!token && refreshError` still fires, so it **also** logs the error and emits `user.auth_refresh_soft_failure`.
4. It returns `undefined`. The controller tries again on its next tick, and the cycle repeats.

The stored credentials never change during this loop. A reauth rejection does not clear them (the user has to sign in again), so every poll re-sends the same rejected token. The cost goes beyond telemetry noise: each affected machine sends a refresh request to the auth server every ~12s for as long as the hub runs.

Before 0.2.0 the hub had no cloud poller calling into the refresh path, which is why 0.0.95 sees ~1 `user.auth_logged_out` per signed-out machine.

#### Fix

`getAuthToken` now remembers which credentials were rejected:

- On `OAuthReauthRequiredError`, it records a fingerprint of the stored Cline credentials (access token, refresh token, `expiresAt`, `apiKey`, `baseUrl`) in a closure-local `rejectedCredentials`, and returns `undefined`.
- On the next call, if the stored credentials still match that fingerprint, it returns `undefined` immediately, with no refresh request and no telemetry.
- As soon as anything changes the stored credentials (signing in again, signing out, a token rotation from another client writing to the shared provider settings), the fingerprint no longer matches. The rejection is then cleared and the next poll refreshes normally.
- A rejection no longer emits `user.auth_refresh_soft_failure`. The refresh path has already reported it once as `user.auth_logged_out`, which is the accurate event. It's not a soft failure, because no fallback could succeed.
- **Transient failures** (network errors, 5xx) work exactly as before: each poll retries, falls back to the stored key, and reports a soft failure if that also fails.

```ts
const credentials = credentialFingerprint(this.settings.getProviderSettings("cline"));
if (credentials === rejectedCredentials) return undefined;
rejectedCredentials = undefined;
// ...refresh...
if (refreshError instanceof OAuthReauthRequiredError) {
  rejectedCredentials = credentials;
  ...
  return undefined;
}
```

#### Decisions and alternatives

- **Why a fingerprint of the stored credentials, not a timer or backoff?** A rejected refresh token never becomes valid again, so a backoff only lowers the rate of a pointless request. Comparing against the stored credentials is exact: the hub stops refreshing for as long as nothing changes, and recovers on the very next poll after the user signs in. No sign-in event has to be wired through to the service.
- **Why the fingerprint includes the access token and `expiresAt`, not just the refresh token:** any write to the credentials should count as "maybe valid now". Over-invalidating costs at most one extra refresh. Under-invalidating would leave a freshly signed-in user stuck.
- **The fingerprint stays in memory only.** It's a string compared within one closure and is never serialized or logged, the same handling the existing `CloudAccountScope` gets.
- **Why not stop the controller on rejection?** That's a larger lifecycle change. The controller would have to be restarted on sign-in, and scope changes already drive that through `isCurrentScope`. Returning `undefined` already makes the controller treat the account as signed out. The only problem was the side effects of getting there on every poll.
- **Why not fix it in `RuntimeOAuthTokenManager`?** Other callers, such as the VSCode, CLI and desktop request paths, refresh on demand, in response to a user action. There, re-trying after a rejection is reasonable, and the logout event they emit is accurate. The every-12-seconds amplification is specific to this poller.
- The scope check after a rejection is kept: if the account changed during the refresh, the caller still gets `Cline account changed` rather than a silent `undefined`.

### Test Procedure

`sdk/packages/core`: `vitest run src/hub/server/cloud-session-service.test.ts`. All 34 tests pass, including two new ones:

- **"stops refreshing rejected credentials until they change"**:
  - 5 polls with rejected credentials make exactly 1 refresh call, and no `user.auth_refresh_soft_failure` is captured.
  - Then the stored credentials are swapped for new ones, as after a fresh sign-in. The next poll refreshes and returns the new key.
- **"keeps reporting refresh failures that are not a rejection"**: a generic error is retried on every poll, as before.

With the fix reverted, the first test fails (5 refresh calls instead of 1), so it reproduces the shipped bug.

`biome check` and `tsc` are clean.

**After release**, on core versions that include this fix:

- hub `user.auth_logged_out` should be back to ~1 per signed-out machine;
- `user.auth_refresh_soft_failure` with `OAuthReauthRequiredError` should drop to ~0;
- hub errors per task should return to the 1.4–1.9 range.

title: fix(llms): back off between in-stream provider retries
body:
## Cause

The AI SDK's `streamRetries` re-dials the moment a provider error part arrives, with no wait between attempts. A provider that is overloaded is still overloaded a few milliseconds later, so all four attempts fail the same way and the user sees the provider's message ("Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later.") with a manual Retry button. In telemetry for 4.1.25 (Oct 20–23), 54% of the overload failures that reached users came through this path, and when users retried by hand 2–10 s later, 81% of those retries succeeded.

Two smaller problems on the same path:

- Capacity errors from OpenAI-compatible backends arrive as in-band error parts with no HTTP status. The AI SDK recognises only a few exact messages, so it types these as non-retryable, and our classifier had neither their provider codes nor a message fallback for them.
- The silent retry attempts left no telemetry, so no retry policy could be measured.

## Changes

- `stream-retry-backoff.ts`: `onError` now waits 1 s, 2 s, 4 s (cap 8 s) before the AI SDK's next in-stream attempt; the SDK awaits `onError` before re-dialing. No wait when no stream retry follows (request-start `RetryError`, transport failures, tool-choice violations) or when the failure reproduces on every attempt (credential, context window). Vendors can tune or disable it through `ProviderFactoryResult.streamRetryBackoff`.
- The wait is announced through `emitStatusNotice` ("provider error — retrying in 2s (attempt 2/3)"), which renders as an info row in VS Code and JetBrains and as a status line in the CLI. `GatewayStreamRequest` carries the callback from the agent runtime.
- `error-classification.ts`: provider capacity codes (`server_is_overloaded`, `service_unavailable`, `service_unavailable_error`, `overloaded`, `overloaded_error`, `model_overloaded`) and an `overloaded` message fallback count as retryable when no status is present.
- Telemetry: an `sdk.stream_retry` event per wait; the terminal `sdk.error` carries `streamRetryAttempts` and `streamRetryWaitMs`.
- `sleep` moved out of the empty-response middleware into its own module, shared with the backoff.

Fixes https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/13356 ([CLINE-3015](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3015/error-our-servers-are-currently-overloaded-please-try-again-later)); the same failure was reported in a JetBrains Marketplace review on 2026-08-19.
Refs https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/13606 ([CLINE-3088](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3088/task-aborts-on-transient-api-errors-timeouts-provider-outages-instead)) and [ENG-2350](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/ENG-2350/decision-auto-retry-parity-was-dropped-entirely-restore-or-accept). Request-start failures that exhaust the SDK's own `maxRetries` backoff (the other 46% of overload failures) are out of scope here.

## Tests

```bash
cd sdk/packages/llms && bunx vitest run src/providers/stream-retry-backoff.test.ts src/providers/gateway.test.ts src/providers/error-classification.test.ts src/providers/ai-sdk.stream-retry-backoff.test.ts
```

`ai-sdk.stream-retry-backoff.test.ts` drives the real `ai` package over the OpenAI-compatible wire format: an overloaded error frame, then a successful stream. It asserts that the re-dial waits, that the notice is emitted once, and that the retry's text is what the caller receives.

## Release note

Transient provider errors during a response (such as "servers are currently overloaded") are now retried with a short backoff and shown as a retry notice, instead of failing the request after four immediate attempts.

title: fix(webview): open chat links to local files in the editor
body:
Part of [CLINE-3681](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3681/cline-html-file-can-be-opened-within-cline-app-and-messed-up-whole-ui) (https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/issues/1241). The JetBrains side, which stops such a click from replacing the panel, is https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/pull/1243.

## Problem

When the model links a local file in a chat message, e.g. `[Open index.html](/Users/me/project/index.html)`, `MarkdownBlock` rendered a plain anchor and left the click to the host. VS Code's webview drops it (only `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `vscode` links are opened), so nothing happened. The JetBrains webview navigated to the resolved URL and lost the panel.

The host cannot do better: by the time the click is a navigation, the href has been through react-markdown's URL sanitising, which blanks `file:` URLs and `C:\` paths as unknown schemes, and through URL resolution against the webview origin, which turns `\\server\share` into `https://server/share`. The webview is the only place where the href the model wrote is still known.

## Change

- `localFileLink(href)` classifies an href as a link to a local file: an absolute POSIX, Windows or UNC path, a `file:` URL, or a scheme-less path relative to the workspace. Web links, other schemes and anchors are left alone. The markdown parser percent-encodes the destination (`C:\x` arrives as `C:%5Cx`, a space as `%20`), so a path is decoded back to what was written; a `file:` URL is passed on as is.
- `MarkdownBlock` keeps those hrefs through `urlTransform` and renders them with a click handler that opens the file through `FileService.openFile` (absolute, `file:`) or `openFileRelativePath` (relative) instead of navigating. The anchor's tooltip names the path. Other links keep their default behaviour.
- `openFile` in `integrations/misc/open-file.ts` turns a `file:` URL into the platform's path with `fileURLToPath`, so drive letters and UNC hosts are interpreted where the file lives. A file that cannot be opened still shows "Could not open file!".

## Testing

- `webview-ui`: `localFileLink.spec.ts` (classification, decoding, `file:` passthrough) and `MarkdownBlock.spec.tsx`, which renders real markdown through the component and checks the href, that the click is prevented, and which RPC is called with what.
- `open-file.test.ts`: absolute path passed through, `file:` URL converted.
- VS Code dev host on macOS: a model reply with five links. Absolute path, relative path and `file:` URL each opened the file in an editor tab; a `C:\...` path reached core as written and showed "Could not open file!" (expected on macOS); the `https` link opened the browser. The panel kept its state.
- JetBrains sandbox (IU 2025.1.7, with https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/pull/1243): the same five links; absolute, relative and `file:` open the file through the host bridge, the Windows path shows "Could not open file!", the `https` link goes to the external browser, the panel keeps its state.
- Not run: Windows. The Windows and UNC cases are covered by the unit tests; the path reaches core unchanged and Node resolves it there.

```bash
cd webview-ui && bunx vitest run src/utils/__tests__/localFileLink.spec.ts src/components/common/__tests__/MarkdownBlock.spec.tsx
bun test src/integrations/misc/open-file.test.ts
```

## Release note

Links to local files in Cline's chat open the file in the editor.

title: fix(core): treat a 404/402 from the current-plan endpoint as no plan
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** none filed; found during a post-release telemetry check of desktop 0.0.49 / core 0.2.0.

### Description

#### What telemetry showed

In the first hours after the Oct 26 release, desktop 0.0.49 logged a new error, `no plan history found for user`, from the `cline_account` sidecar command:

- **135 signed-in machines in 3 hours, ~9% of all 0.0.49 machines**, ~2 events each.
- **Zero on 0.0.48.**

It's the only new error type in the release with that kind of reach. It's not a crash, but it inflates desktop error counts and puts the Account view on an error path for free users.

#### Cause

`GET /api/v1/users/me/plan` answers:

- **404** with `{"success":false,"error":"no plan history found for user"}` for anyone who has never had a plan;
- **402** when the plan is unpaid.

Both mean "not subscribed". `ClineAccountService.fetchCurrentUserPlan` (core) didn't distinguish them from a real failure. `request()` throws on any non-2xx, so every caller got a rejected promise.

- **Desktop:** `fetchClinePassModels` in `account-view.tsx` is written to return `null` when there's no plan (`plan?.plan?.entitlements`). It never got the chance, because the invoke rejected first, and the sidecar captured the failure as an `sdk.error`. The call became more prominent in 0.0.49, which is why the error appeared with this release.
- **CLI:** onboarding (`tui/views/onboarding/controller.ts`) already worked around this by string-matching the error message: `message === "no plan found for user"` → unsubscribed. **The API now says `no plan history found for user`**, so that match no longer fires and unsubscribed users land in the ClinePass *error* state instead of *unsubscribed*. That's a second, silent bug with the same root cause.
- **VSCode** was never affected. Its own account service (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/account-service.ts`, `fetchClinePassSubscribedRPC`) maps 404 and 402 to "not subscribed" and has a test for exactly that.

#### Fix

`request()` gains an `absentOnStatus` option: listed statuses resolve `undefined` instead of throwing, checked before the body is parsed. `fetchCurrentUserPlan` passes `[402, 404]`.

The return type was already `Promise<UserCurrentPlan | undefined>`, so every caller already handles `undefined` as "no plan":

- desktop's `fetchClinePassModels` returns `null`;
- CLI onboarding's fulfilled branch sets `"unsubscribed"` when `value?.plan` is empty.

No caller changes are needed. Other failures (401, 5xx, network, timeout) still throw exactly as before.

Why fix it in core rather than in each caller:

- one place, matching VSCode's semantics;
- removes the reliance on the API's error wording that broke the CLI;
- every other `fetchCurrentUserPlan` consumer gets the right behaviour for free.

The CLI's string match is now dead code for this case. I left it alone to keep the diff to the root cause; it's harmless and can go in a follow-up.

### Test Procedure

- `sdk/packages/core`: `vitest run src/account`: 4 files, 26 tests pass. New cases:
  - 404 with the real `no plan history found for user` envelope resolves `undefined`;
  - 402 resolves `undefined`;

- `apps/cli`: `vitest run src/tui/cline-account.test.ts`: 9 tests pass.
- `biome check` is clean on both files, and `tsc` reports no errors in `src/account`.

**After release:** desktop `sdk.error` events with `no plan history found for user` should drop to zero on the next desktop build.

title: fix(llms): keep Anthropic prompt cache advancing through tool loops
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15307 (also #15167)

### Description

With the direct Anthropic provider, prompt caching stopped advancing during tool-call loops. Cache reads stayed flat at the size of the first prompt and nothing new was written, so every tool step was billed at the full input rate.

Cause: `buildAnthropicProviderOptions` set the request-level option as `cache_control`. `@ai-sdk/anthropic` strips that key. Only `cacheControl` gets mapped to the top-level `cache_control` that turns on Anthropic's automatic caching, which moves the cache point forward on each turn. Without it, the only breakpoint was the explicit one on the last `user` message. Tool results are sent as `tool` messages, so during a loop that breakpoint stayed on the original prompt.

The Cline and OpenRouter paths were not affected, because the openai-compatible passthrough already sends a top-level `cache_control`.

The fix gives `createEphemeralCacheControl()` an optional key parameter that defaults to the `cache_control` wire field. The Anthropic request-level option now calls it with `"cacheControl"`. All other callers and the per-part markers are unchanged, since the AI SDK accepts both spellings on parts. This is a much smaller alternative to #15174 with the same result.

| Request | Before: cache read / write | After: cache read / write |
|---|---|---|
| Initial prompt | 0 / 3,359 | 0 / 3,361 |
| After 1 tool round | 3,359 / 0 | 3,361 / 3,187 |
| After 2 tool rounds | 3,359 / 0 | 6,548 / 3,188 |
| After 3 tool rounds | 3,359 / 0 | 9,736 / 3,188 |

### Additional Notes

Requests now carry two breakpoints: the explicit one on the last user text and the automatic one. That is within Anthropic's limit of 4. Vertex Claude uses the same `anthropic` options bucket, so it will send the top-level flag as well. I did not test Vertex live.

title: feat(cli): send a task to Cline Cloud with --cloud
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (follow-up to #15317, stacked on it)

### Description

Adds `cline --cloud "..."` for sending a task straight to Cline Cloud without opening the TUI. It starts a new cloud session for this folder's GitHub repo (or the one passed with `--repo`), sends the prompt, and exits as soon as the sandbox accepts it, printing a link to follow along. The task keeps running in the cloud after the CLI exits, like `--zen` does for the local Hub.

```sh
cline --cloud "Fix the flaky retry test and open a PR"
git diff | cline --cloud "Review this change"
cline --cloud --repo cline/cline --branch main "Summarize the open TODOs"
```

How it picks things (same rules as the TUI's Cloud mode):
- **Repository:** this folder's git `origin`, which must be a GitHub repo the Cline account can access. `--repo owner/name` (a GitHub URL also works) overrides it, so `--cloud` works from any folder. Clear errors when there's no GitHub repo to use, the `--repo` value isn't a repo, GitHub isn't connected, or the account can't access that repo (with the access link).
- **Branch:** `--branch name` if given, checked against GitHub so a typo fails clearly. Otherwise the current local branch if it exists on GitHub (only when the repo is this folder's origin), otherwise the repo's default branch.
- **Model:** the saved cloud pick from the TUI's `/model`, otherwise the local Cline/ClinePass model if the cloud offers it (so `-m` works too), otherwise ClinePass for ClinePass users, otherwise `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`. This logic moved into a shared `resolveCloudModel()` that the TUI hook now uses as well.
- **Mode:** Act with tools auto-approved in the sandbox.

Details:

title: fix(desktop): use '+' in the Linux nightly version so the rpm bundler accepts it
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A. Found when nightly run [40230534877](https://github.com/cline/cline/actions/runs/40230534877) failed.

### Description

**Problem.** Every desktop nightly now fails in `Build Linux`. The arm64 leg failed, and fail-fast cancelled x64:

```
failed to bundle project: invalid version "0.0.48-nightly.20261025202349.40230534877.1":
contains invalid character (allowed: alphanumeric, '.', '_', '+', '%', '{', '}', '~', '^')
```

**Why now.** #15278 bumped `@tauri-apps/cli` to 2.12.3 for the much faster rpm bundler. The new bundler checks the rpm `Version` tag, and rpm doesn't allow `-` there because it separates version from release. The old bundler wrote whatever it was given. The nightly version is `<base>-nightly.<stamp>.<run id>.<attempt>`, so it always has a `-`. The last nightly that passed (Oct 17, `a42df8c8d5`) was built before #15278, so this is the first nightly on the new CLI. Stable versions like `0.0.48` have no `-`, so stable releases are unaffected.

**Fix.** The Linux job's `Stamp nightly version` step now writes the version with its first `-` changed to `+` (`0.0.48+nightly.20261025202349.40230534877.1`) into `package.json` and `tauri.conf.json`. That form:
- is accepted by rpm (`+` is allowed),
- is a valid Debian upstream version,
- is still valid semver, which Tauri requires for `version`.

The workflow's `validate.outputs.version` is unchanged. The artifact filenames in `Collect artifacts`, the macOS and Windows jobs, and the `desktop-nightly-<stamp>` tag derivation in `announce-nightly` (`${VERSION#*-nightly.}`) still use the original `-` form.

**Why `+` works for nightly only.** In semver, `+` starts build metadata, which is ignored when comparing versions. So the installed Linux nightly reports a version equal to the plain base version. For nightly that doesn't matter: the overlay ships empty updater endpoints and no feed ever serves nightlies.

**Known gap: beta has the same problem, and this PR doesn't fix it.** Beta versions (`0.0.49-beta.1`) also contain `-`, so the next beta's Linux build will fail the same way. Using `+` for beta would be wrong. An installed `0.0.49+beta.1` compares equal to `0.0.49`, which is newer than every `0.0.49-beta.N` in the beta feed, so Linux beta users would stop getting updates until the next base version. Tauri has no separate rpm/deb version override, so fixing beta needs a different approach, such as a custom updater version comparator or a different beta version format. Beta has been dormant since `desktop-v0.0.23-beta.1` in early September, so I left it for when beta is next used.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Pinning `@tauri-apps/cli` back below 2.12: this undoes #15278's large speedup to the Linux rpm build, which was taking 26–30 minutes.
- `~` (rpm's prerelease convention): not valid semver, so Tauri would reject it in `tauri.conf.json`.

### Test Procedure

- Parsed the workflow YAML (`Bun.YAML.parse`) to confirm it's still valid.
- Confirmed the rewrite produces `0.0.48+nightly.20261025202349.40230534877.1`, which uses only characters the bundler's error message lists as allowed.
- Checked every `VERSION` reference in `build-linux`. Only the stamp step and `Collect artifacts` (which uses the shared, unmodified version for filenames) read it. Nothing in the job compares the built version to the expected one.
- The real test is the next nightly after merge, which should produce `desktop-linux-x64` and `desktop-linux-arm64` artifacts.

title: fix(compaction): correct the context-size estimate in both directions
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14979

### Description

Auto-compaction fired far below the real context window when the char-based token estimate overshot the provider's actual input count.

The correction in `compaction.ts` computes `actual / estimate` from the provider's previous request count, but clamps it with `Math.max(1, ...)`. A factor can only tighten the budget (estimate under-counting), never loosen it. With prose-heavy transcripts the chars/3 estimate reads ~1.5x the real tokens, so the trigger tripped near 60% of the real window.

Changes:

- `compaction.ts`: clamp the correction ratio between a new `MIN_INPUT_OVERESTIMATE_FACTOR` (0.5) and the existing `MAX_INPUT_UNDERESTIMATE_FACTOR` (4). A count above the estimate still tightens; a count below it now loosens up to 2x. Renamed the variable and debug field to `estimateCorrectionFactor` since it is no longer one-sided.
- `compaction-shared.ts`: added `MIN_INPUT_OVERESTIMATE_FACTOR` with a comment explaining the bound.

The floor mirrors the existing cap: a wildly inflated estimate cannot push compaction past the real window.

title: fix(hooks): run UserPromptSubmit hooks for prompts seeded into the runtime
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14963

### Description

UserPromptSubmit hooks never ran for the user's actual message in CLI and desktop sessions.

Two different paths deliver the prompt to `AgentRuntime`:

1. A directly driven runtime gets the prompt as `run(input)` and emits it as `message-added`.
2. Orchestrated sessions (what the CLI and desktop use) append the user message to the conversation, seed it into `initialMessages`, and call `run("")`. No `message-added` event fires for that prompt.

The file hook layer only dispatched `prompt_submit` from `message-added`, so path 2 never fired the hook. The VS Code hooks adapter already handles this by scanning the `beforeRun` snapshot; this change does the same at the core file-hook layer and in the CLI's in-process hook dispatcher.

Changes:

- `createHookConfigFileHooks` now installs `beforeRun` when prompt_submit hooks exist and scans the snapshot for the latest user message that is not marked `displayRole: "system"`, dispatching `prompt_submit` there. If a run-start hook cancels the run, the prompt hook is skipped, matching the extension.
- `onEvent` keeps handling `message-added` for directly driven runtimes. Dispatched message ids are tracked so a `continue()` run, whose snapshot still contains earlier prompts, does not re-fire them.
- The audit hook layer records the same prompt_submit dispatch so `hooks.jsonl` reflects what the file hooks actually ran.
- Runtime-generated user-role reminders (completion-tool reminder, completion policy reminders, max-tokens recovery nudge, unexpected-turn continuation) are now marked `displayRole: "system"` so the snapshot scan does not mistake them for user prompts.
- The CLI's in-process hook dispatcher in `apps/cli/src/utils/hooks.ts` gets the same snapshot scan and dedup.

### Test Procedure

title: cli: publish musl builds for Linux
body:
Refs #15271.

## What

Adds musl Linux to the CLI's build matrix and publishes two more platform packages:

- `@cline/cli-linux-x64-musl`
- `@cline/cli-linux-arm64-musl`

The glibc Linux packages additionally get `"libc": ["glibc"]`, and the musl ones
`"libc": ["musl"]`, so npm's libc-aware optional dependency resolution
(npm >= 10.4) installs the right binary on each host instead of pulling in a
glibc build that dies in the loader.

## Why it was more than one line

Bun compiles these targets from any host (`bun-linux-{x64,arm64}-musl`), and
`@opentui/core` already ships `core-linux-{x64,arm64}-musl`. Two things were
still missing:

1. **OpenTUI picks its native library at runtime** from `OPENTUI_LIBC`,
   defaulting to glibc. A musl binary therefore extracted and loaded the glibc
   `.so` and failed with `Error loading shared library ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`.
   The target's libc is now baked in with a `define`, which also lets Bun
   tree-shake the variant it will never load (156 MB -> 143 MB).
2. **The npm wrapper and `postinstall.mjs` hard-code**
   `@cline/cli-<os>-<arch>`. Both now append `-musl` when the running Node has
   no glibc runtime, using Node's diagnostic report.

## Testing

Built all eight targets with the patched script (`bun script/build.ts
--install-native-variants --skip-sdk-build`, ~2 minutes) and ran the
`@cline/cli-linux-x64-musl` binary on **OpenWrt 24.10.8 / x86_64 / musl**
(`libstdcpp6` installed, which is the only extra system dependency — Bun's
musl runtime links `libstdc++.so.6`):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cline --version` | `3.0.73`, 0.8 s |
| `cline hub start` / `status` / `stop` | running, coreVersion `0.2.0` |
| TUI (opentui render library) | renders the welcome screen |
| peak RSS (TUI) | ~230 MB |

`bun biome check` and `bun -F @cline/cli typecheck` pass. The arm64 musl
binary builds and links against `/lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1`, but I have not
run it on aarch64 hardware yet.

Note for the release workflow: musl binaries still need `libstdc++` on the
target system (a 643 KB package on OpenWrt). If you would rather not carry that
dependency, it can be documented or handled in a follow-up — the build itself
does not change.

bun -F @cline/agents test
bun -F @cline/llms test
bun run build:sdk
bun -F @cline/cli build

The regression tests feed Gemini SSE responses through a custom fetch, exercising the gateway and Agent loop without network access or provider credentials.

title: feat(desktop): separate Changes pane and a last-turn receipt in the transcript
body:
### Related Issue

N/A (internal feature work, follow-up to #14956)

### Description

The project files panel (#14956) answers "browse or commit my repo", but not "what did the agent just do". Its Git view shows the whole uncommitted working tree, so the agent's edits are mixed with your own and with earlier sessions, and there was no way to see what the last turn changed.

This splits the two questions into two controls and adds an entry point from the chat:

- **Header:** a **Changes** button carrying the session's line counts, and the folder button (now icon-only) for the existing Files + Git panel. Both open in the same right-hand slot.
- **Changes pane:** `Last turn | Session` tabs, a file list (same rows as the Git view), and a diff of the selected file. A footer link, **All uncommitted changes**, jumps to the Git view. Without git checkpoints (plain folders, SSH) it falls back to the tool-event reconstruction of the session with a notice.
- **Receipt:** when the last turn finishes, a small card under it lists what it changed (`Changed 1 file +1 -0`). Clicking it, or one of its files, opens the pane on Last turn. Sending the next message removes it; a new one appears when that turn finishes.

**How changes are computed (sidecar, `session-changes.ts`).** Core already writes a git checkpoint before each turn's first model call. The last turn is the latest checkpoint against the working tree; the session is the first checkpoint against the working tree. Each point becomes a git tree:
- a checkpoint's tree overlaid with its untracked-files third parent (`git read-tree <tree> <untracked-tree>` into a temp index), so files the agent created but never staged are included;
- the working tree via a temp copy of the real index plus `git add -A`, which keeps the stat cache and never touches the real index.

Then `git diff-tree --raw` / `--numstat` gives paths, statuses, and line counts. `read_session_change` returns both sides of one change by blob id (1 MiB cap, binary-aware, object ids validated). Both commands require the trusted desktop connection, like source control.

Supporting refactors: the panel's width tracking and drag handle moved into `WorkspacePanelFrame` (shared by both panels), and the Git view's `ChangeRow` is exported with optional actions.

Not included: an "Uncommitted" scope (it duplicates the Git view), revert/undo, and reviewing older individual turns.

### Test Procedure

- `sidecar/session-changes.test.ts` builds real temp repos with stash-shaped checkpoints (including the untracked third parent) and checks the last-turn and session diffs, that a pre-existing untracked file never shows, that the real index is untouched, binary handling, and object id validation.
- New `changes-panel.test.tsx` (two scopes, blob reads, Git/close callbacks, tool-event fallback forcing Session), receipt cases in `chat-messages.test.tsx` (shown after the finished last turn, hidden while running and once a new user message exists), and updated `agent-header.test.tsx` for the two-button header.

- Manual: ran a real multi-turn agent session in a demo repo that already had an uncommitted edit of mine, then opened it in the headless desktop app. One receipt sat under the last turn, my pre-existing edit stayed out of the session view, Review opened Last turn, sending a new message removed the receipt immediately, and a new receipt appeared when that turn finished.

Receipt under the finished last turn:

![Last turn receipt in the transcript](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-2b5b9e53-5b09-42bd-854d-698697c8fb78)

Last turn opened from the receipt:

title: fix(desktop): start Cloud on the local Cline/ClinePass model, else ClinePass or Sonnet 5.5
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (desktop follow-up to #15302)

### Description

Desktop now picks the default model for a new Cloud chat in this order:

0. A Cloud model the user picked in the model picker always wins.
1. Otherwise, the local Cline or ClinePass model, if the Cloud catalog offers it.
2. Otherwise, the first ClinePass model, if the local provider is ClinePass. There is no subscription lookup.
3. Otherwise, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

Before this change:
- Only a local `cline` model carried over.
- If the catalog didn't offer the model, the picker switched to whatever the catalog listed first.
- Every Cloud model change was saved, including automatic fallbacks, so the default froze after the first fallback.

Changes:
- **Fallback:** the Cloud `ModelSelector` replaces a model the catalog doesn't offer with the first ClinePass model when the local provider is ClinePass, otherwise Sonnet 5.5. The local provider is read from the saved local model selection when the Cloud picker mounts. Organization accounts get no ClinePass models from the catalog, so they land on Sonnet 5.5. If Sonnet isn't offered either, the picker keeps the old first-entry fallback so sending isn't blocked.
- **Saving:** only explicit picks are saved. Saving moved out of `handleModelChange` in `page.tsx` and into the picker's explicit-pick handlers, so automatic fallbacks stay defaults and the next Cloud chat follows the current local model. This also removes the now-redundant `persistSelection` prop.
- **Starting model:** `getInitialCloudModel()` is now the single source for both new chats and the Local to Cloud switch. It carries over any local Cline or ClinePass model, including ClinePass free models (`cline-free/...`). Cloud doesn't offer those, so the picker moves them onto ClinePass.
- **Switching Local and Cloud** still never changes either side's model.

### Test Procedure

- `model-selection.test.ts`: starting model for local `cline`, `cline-pass`, a ClinePass free model, and a third-party provider. A saved Cloud pick overrides all of them.
- `chat-input-bar.test.tsx`, new Cloud chat:
  - An offered model is kept.
  - A local ClinePass free model goes to the first ClinePass model.
  - An unoffered model for a local Cline user goes to Sonnet 5.5.
  - A local ClinePass model on an organization account (no ClinePass catalog) goes to Sonnet 5.5.
  - Automatic choices are never saved; explicit picks are.
  - Forcing the ClinePass check off makes the ClinePass case fail.

title: feat(cli): start Cline Cloud sessions from the interactive TUI
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (internal feature, follows the CLI cloud UX mockups)

### Description

Adds the ability to start and use Cline Cloud sessions from the CLI TUI, like the VS Code extension and desktop app already can. It is behind `CLINE_CLOUD_SESSIONS=1` while cloud sessions are experimental.

**UX**
- The status bar gets a new `● Local ○ Cloud (Ctrl+O)` row.
- In Cloud mode, the workspace row becomes `☁ owner/repo · branch (Ctrl+K)`, and `Ctrl+K` reopens the repo/branch picker.
- Cloud sessions always run in Act mode with tools auto-approved in their sandbox, so the Plan/Act toggle and the auto-approve row are hidden in Cloud mode, and `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` do nothing there. Switching to Cloud from Plan flips the UI to Act.
- In Cloud mode, `/model` (and "Change model" in `Ctrl+P`) opens a "Select Cloud Model" picker laid out like the Settings model picker: `Provider: ClinePass (tab to change provider)` above a searchable list of that provider's models. `Tab` opens a "Select Cloud Provider" list with the cloud billing catalogs the desktop app offers (ClinePass, Cline Usage-Billing, ClineFree). The pick shows on the status bar (for example `ClinePass: kimi-k3.1-pro`), is used to create the session, and is sent with every message, so you can switch models mid-session.
- Cloud model choice, matching VS Code (#15302): an explicit `/model` pick in Cloud mode is saved and wins while the cloud catalog offers it. Without one, the default is recomputed each time: your local Cline or ClinePass model if the cloud catalog offers it, otherwise ClinePass if your selected local provider is ClinePass, otherwise Cline's default usage-billed model (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`). Defaults are never saved, so they follow later changes to your local model or provider.
- The first time you pick Cloud, a setup dialog walks through signing in to Cline and connecting GitHub, reusing the extension's wording. After that, a "Run in Cline Cloud" picker opens. It's laid out like Select Model: `Repository: x (tab to change repository)` above a searchable branch list. It defaults to this folder's `origin` repo and to the default or current branch, and branch search runs on the server.
- When you submit, the status row shows the sandbox phases (Starting sandbox, Cloning repository, Starting agent), then Working or Ready in Cline Cloud. The transcript streams in from the cloud session, and follow-up messages go to the same session.
- Once a cloud session starts, the target is locked. `Ctrl+L` returns to a fresh chat with the repo still selected.
- `/compact` and `/fork` act on the local session, so in Cloud mode they show a short "isn't available in Cline Cloud yet" toast instead.

**How it works**
- `runtime/interactive/cloud-sessions.ts` connects a `HubCloudSessionClient` (from `@cline/core/cloud`, #15205) to the shared Hub. The Hub owns credentials, provisioning and sandbox connections.
- `tui/hooks/use-cloud-sessions.tsx` holds the target, repo and model selection, setup flow, create/send/abort, and snapshot projection. The transcript renders from cloud snapshots via the existing `hydrateSessionMessages`, so reconnects and rehydration need no extra handling.
- The explicit cloud model pick is stored as `cloudModelId` in the core global settings (next to `tuiTheme`), via new `readCloudModelIdGlobally`/`setCloudModelIdGlobally` helpers.
- When the feature is off, the status bar, keybinds and `/model` are unchanged.

JC's `/cloud` handoff (moving an existing chat to the cloud) is separate. This PR only covers starting new chats in the cloud, but the picker and status row can be shared with it.

### Test Procedure

- `bun run typecheck`, Biome, and the `apps/cli` unit suite. New tests cover `Ctrl+O`/`Ctrl+K` routing (including leaving both keys to the input when cloud is off), `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` being ignored in Cloud mode, and parsing GitHub repo names from `origin` URLs.
- Manual end-to-end runs in the real TUI with `CLINE_CLOUD_SESSIONS=1` against production with a Cline API key:
  - The sign-in setup dialog appears when not signed in, and Esc returns to Local.
  - The real GitHub repo list and branch list load, server-side branch search works, and picking a branch updates the status bar.
  - Submitting a read-only prompt provisioned a sandbox (phases shown in the status row), ran tools in the cloud without approval prompts, and rendered the reply.
  - A local Cline usage-billing model (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`) was kept as the cloud default. With no offered local model, a local ClinePass provider defaulted to `ClinePass: kimi-k3.1-pro`, and a non-Cline provider (Anthropic) defaulted to `Anthropic: Claude Sonnet 5.5`. `Tab` in the model picker opened the provider list, and choosing Cline Usage-Billing showed its models.
  - Picking Claude Opus 5.5 with `/model` wrote `cloudModelId` to global settings and survived a restart, winning over the local model. With no saved pick, changing the local model to Claude Opus 5.5 mid-run moved the cloud default to it.
  - Sessions ran on ClinePass kimi-k3.1-pro and on Claude Opus 5.5; switching models mid-session and sending a follow-up worked, and the Hub's session state confirmed the new model.
  - `Ctrl+O` shows a toast while a session is active, `Ctrl+L` resets to home with the repo kept, and `Ctrl+K` reopens the picker.
  - Starting in Plan and switching to Cloud flips to Act. Plan/Act and auto-approve hide in Cloud and return in Local.

title: fix(core): connect SSH remotes behind a ProxyJump alias
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14552

### Description

Connecting to an SSH remote whose host is an `ssh_config` alias with `ProxyJump` and a `LocalForward` failed with `EPIPE: broken pipe, write` or `Connection timed out during banner exchange / Connection to UNKNOWN port 65535 timed out`, while Test Connection passed. All three fixes are in `sdk/packages/core/src/remote/remote-environments.ts`:

1. **Connect budget.** OpenSSH's `ConnectTimeout` also bounds the banner exchange. Behind a `ProxyJump`, the connection is a pipe to the inner `ssh -W`, so logging in to the bastion and opening the channel all had to finish within 10 seconds. Test Connection is one session, but connect runs about ten in a row, so one of them often timed out. The budget is now 30s, and the per-command timeout is 60s so the user sees ssh's own message. The tunnel is another ssh session through the same hop, so its readiness limit goes from 10s to 40s.
2. **Upload errors.** When ssh exited while the CLI binary was being uploaded over stdin, the stdin `EPIPE` killed the process and its stderr was lost. Now it stops writing and lets ssh close, so the exit code and stderr are reported. A zero exit before the input was fully written is still rejected (`writableFinished`).
3. **Alias forwardings.** One-shot commands pass `ClearAllForwardings=yes`, the same as `scp` and `sftp`, so they no longer bind the alias's `LocalForward`. The tunnel can't use that option because it would also clear our own `-L`, so it drops `ExitOnForwardFailure` instead. A bind collision on the alias's forwarding is now only a warning, and `waitForTunnel` still checks our forward.

### Test Procedure

- `vitest run src/remote/` in `@cline/core`: 56 passed, 5 consecutive runs. The two new `runRemoteProcess` tests (ssh exits mid-upload with stderr; a zero exit before reading input) fail against `main` and pass here. `biome check` is clean. `tsc` reports only an existing error in `hub-upgrades.test.ts`, which is also on `main`.
- End to end with real OpenSSH in a VM, using a freshly built Cline CLI as the uploaded binary. Setup: two user-mode `sshd` instances (bastion and target), an alias routed through the bastion with a `LocalForward 127.0.0.1:8380`, and port 8380 held by another process.
  - `main`: `SSH tunnel exited before it became ready (exit 255)`.
  - This branch: connect (upload, `cline hub ensure`, tunnel), then run, then disconnect all succeed, and no Hub process is left behind.
  - A jump hop slower than the budget (scaled down to a 3s hop with a 2s budget) reports ssh's `Connection timed out during banner exchange` both before and during the upload, not `EPIPE`. The same hop connects with the default budget.

title: fix(cli): detect npx installs from the Windows npm cache layout
body:
## Summary

`getInstallationInfo` resolves the package manager from the wrapper path, but the npx patterns only match the macOS/Linux npm cache layout (`~/.npm/_npx/...`). On Windows the npx cache lives at `%LocalAppData%\npm-cache\_npx\...`, which does not contain the `/npm/_npx` substring, so `npx cline` falls through to the `/node_modules/` check and is misdetected as a global **npm** install.

Consequences for Windows `npx cline` users:

- `cline update` runs `npm update -g cline --tag latest --min-release-age=0`, creating a global npm installation the user never asked for.
- The exit-time auto update (`applyDeferredUpdate`) can run that same global install silently in the background once no other CLI is attached to the hub.
- `getPreferredKanbanInstaller` resolves to `"npm"`, so kanban installs are also pointed at npm.

On macOS/Linux detection correctly returns `NPX` (no update command, auto update skipped), so this is a Windows-only divergence.

## Changes

- Add `/npm-cache/_npx` to the npx detection patterns in `getInstallationInfo` (one extra condition, same style as the existing alternatives).
- Add vitest cases for both the macOS `.npm/_npx` layout (existing behavior, previously untested) and the Windows `npm-cache/_npx` layout.

## Testing

- Detection matrix verified standalone: Windows npx caches (npm v6/v7 layouts) flip `NPM` -> `NPX`; global npm, pnpm-global Windows, and macOS npx detections are unchanged.
- The two added vitest cases in `update.test.ts` run in CI.

Related context: #13115 (update failure on global npm installs) and #12224 (bun global detection) are the same detection area but distinct issues. Yarn Classic global installs on Windows (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Yarn\...`, capital Y) also miss the `/yarn/global` pattern; left out to keep this change minimal, happy to follow up if preferred.

title: fix(cli): reject malformed integer values in hub --port and connector flags

## Summary

Companion to #15297 (which fixed the CLI's `--timeout` / `--retries` / `--limit` / schedule flags): three more integer parsers in the CLI silently truncate malformed input through `Number.parseInt` instead of rejecting it.

- `commands/hub.ts`: the `--port` option parser returned `Number.parseInt(value, 10)`, so `--port 8080x` became `8080` and `--port abc` became `NaN`. It now throws `InvalidArgumentError` for anything that is not a plain non-negative integer, matching the existing `parseWaitSeconds` pattern in the same file.
- `connectors/base.ts`: `parseOptionalInteger` (used by the discord / gchat / linear / slack / whatsapp adapters for `--port`) accepted `8080x` → `8080`, `0x10` → `0`, and `-1`. It now requires a plain non-negative integer and keeps the existing `invalid port "..."` error message.
- `wizards/schedule/index.ts`: the advanced-options wizard parsed `Timeout` / `Max iterations` with `Number.parseInt` and silently truncated what it could not fully read, so typing `10m` configured a 10-second timeout. Both prompts now use the same `validate` convention the other prompts in that wizard already have.

## Changes

- Strict digit validation in the three sites above; valid inputs are unchanged (`8080`, `" 8080 "`, `25463` still parse the same).

## Testing

- `hub.test.ts`: `ensure --port 8080x` now rejects and never starts the daemon; `ensure --port 25463` still parses and forwards `port: 25463`.
- `base.test.ts`: `parseOptionalInteger` accepts integers/whitespace/`undefined`, and rejects `8080x`, `8o80`, `-1`, `1.5`, `""`, `0x10` with the unchanged `invalid port "..."` message.

**Issue:** N/A (release process cleanup)

### Description

`@cline/ui` lives in `sdk/packages/` but was released on its own: a separate `ui-publish.yml` workflow, a separate `publish-ui` skill, and its own version (`0.1.0` / `0.2.0-next.N`). - All SDK packages move from `0.0.95` to `0.2.0` (see Versioning below).
- `sdk-publish.yml`: publish `@cline/ui` after `@cline/sdk` (it only depends on `shared`, so going last keeps the core SDK packages from being half-published if the UI step fails), and add the `sdk/ui/vX.Y.Z` tag and summary line.
- `sdk/scripts/release.ts`: add `ui` to `SDK_PUBLISH_ORDER`.
- `sdk-test.yml`: add the two UI gates from `ui-publish.yml` that SDK CI did not already cover: `bun -F @cline/code test:chat-ui` and the packed-package smoke test (`smoke-package.ts`, Bun/React 19 + npm/React 18). - `smoke-package.ts`: pack the local `@cline/shared` and install it in both consumers, so the smoke test works when the bumped `shared` version is not on npm yet (which is always the case during a release).

title: fix(desktop): send the resumed transcript to the hub once
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15203

### Description

Resuming a desktop session whose transcript is over ~8 MiB fails every time with `Hub connection closed (code=1006, reason=Connection ended)`, and the hub log says `Received too big message`.

The sidecar put the transcript inside the session config (via `buildCoreSessionConfig` and the start path's `coreConfig`) and also passed it as top-level `initialMessages` to `manager.start()`. The hub runtime sends both in one `session.create` frame, so the transcript crossed the wire twice and hit the hub's 16 MiB frame limit at about half the size it should.

Core never reads `initialMessages` from the session config: `LocalRuntimeHost.startSession` reads `input.initialMessages`, and the hub's `session.create` handler reads `payload.initialMessages`. This PR drops the config copy, so only the top-level field is sent. That doubles the size of session that can be resumed (to roughly 16 MiB of messages).

Out of scope: sessions above ~16 MiB still need chunked or lazy transcript loading, and the UI still shows "Connection ended" instead of the real cause. This also helps the other open reports of the same failure (#14707, #14822, #15029, #15091).

- Added an assertion to the existing `chat-session.test.ts` resume test that the start config carries no `initialMessages`. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (internal UX follow-up for cloud sessions)

### Description

In a cloud session, clicking the model label under the chat box opened the normal provider settings. Those settings change the local Plan/Act model, and there was no visible way to choose the model a cloud task runs on. Before this change, the cloud model was derived quietly: the Act-mode Cline model if your Act provider was Cline, otherwise the top recommended Cline model.

This PR adds a **Local | Cloud** toggle to Settings > API Configuration. It only appears when cloud sessions are on.

- **Local** shows the existing provider settings, including the Plan/Act tabs, unchanged.
- **Cloud** shows a Cline model picker with the same catalogs as the desktop app and Cline on the web: **Usage-Billing** (recommended cards, billed to Cline credits), **ClinePass** (subscription models), and **ClineFree** (the cloud-only free list). Search covers the full Usage-Billing catalog plus the ClinePass and ClineFree lists. It opens on the tab that holds the selected model. The choice is saved separately from your local models and applies to new cloud tasks. If a cloud task is open, a note shows the model that task is running on, since a running sandbox can't switch models.
- **ClinePass** is hidden for organization accounts, in self-hosted mode, and when an organization's provider allowlist excludes it (the same gating as the other ClinePass surfaces). For personal accounts without a ClinePass subscription, the tab stays visible and shows a notice with a **Subscribe** link above the models.
- **Cloud model**, picked in this order:
  1. Your saved cloud pick from Settings, if the cloud catalog offers it.
  2. Your local (Act-mode) Cline or ClinePass model, if the cloud catalog offers it.
  3. If your local provider is ClinePass, the first ClinePass model.
  4. Otherwise, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

  Once the plan check says the account has no ClinePass plan, steps 2 and 3 skip ClinePass models, since the cloud refuses them without one (403); a saved Settings pick is still respected. While the plan check hasn't answered (or can't), ClinePass defaults stand. Until the catalog loads (or if it can't), the saved pick and a local Cline model or `cline-pass/` model are assumed to be offered, so the label doesn't flicker for the common case.
- The section opens on whichever side matches the chat view. Clicking the composer's model label from a cloud session (or with Cloud chosen on the home screen) lands on the Cloud tab; from a local session it lands on Local.
- The home screen's Run Task blurb no longer says every cloud task uses Cline credits.

Implementation:
- New `cloudModelId` global-state key and a `CloudService.setCloudModel` RPC.
- `nextCloudModelId()` applies the order above. The cloud coordinator loads the catalog with the SDK's `loadCloudModels` (the same call the desktop app's cloud picker uses; organization accounts get no ClinePass models), once per account. This replaces the recommended-feed warmup it used before.
- The webview receives `nextCloudModelId` alongside the existing `cloudModelId` (the displayed task's model).
- `ClineModelPicker` takes an optional `cloudSelection` so it can edit the cloud model instead of the Plan/Act one and show the cloud tabs. In that mode it hides Reasoning Effort, because that control writes the local Cline provider config.
- The SDK's `fetchClineRecommendedModels` now keeps the feed's `clineCloud` list (it already parsed `clinePass`), and the extension's recommended-models RPC passes it through. Cloud tasks still start with provider `cline` and the prefixed model id (`cline-pass/...`, `cline-cloud/...`), the same way the desktop app does.
- ClinePass subscription: the cloud coordinator checks `/api/v1/users/me/plan` once per account. A plan means subscribed; a 404 (no current plan) or 402 (unpaid plan) means not subscribed; organization accounts count as not subscribed. Any other failure leaves the status unknown, so no notice is shown. The coordinator posts the answer as `clinePassSubscribed` for the Settings notice, and steps 2 and 3 above use it to keep no-plan users off ClinePass. A new `CloudService.refreshClinePassSubscription` RPC re-checks the plan when the Settings Cloud tab opens (an answer under a minute old is reused), so a subscription bought from the Subscribe link shows up without a reload.
- A ClinePass cloud model reads `cline-pass:<model>` in the composer, like a local ClinePass model.
- The toggle reuses the home-screen Run Task Local/Cloud button.

### Test Procedure

- `bun run check-types` and `bun run lint` in `apps/vscode`, `bun run types` in `sdk`, and `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/cli` (it consumes the SDK recommended-models type).
- vitest: the full extension suite. New cases:
  - The Settings cloud model wins over the Act-mode Cline model.
  - Default model:
    - A Settings pick wins when the catalog offers it (or before the catalog loads), and falls through when the catalog no longer offers it.

title: fix(core): read checkpoint diff contents with one git process instead of one per file
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15116

### Description

When a task completes, VS Code renders the "View Changes" row, which calls `checkpointLatestChangesCount`. That runs `buildCheckpointWorkspaceDiff` in `@cline/core`. For every candidate path, it ran `git show <ref>:<path>` and, when that failed, a second `git show <ref>^3:<path>`. All of these ran at once through `Promise.all`.

Checkpoints capture every untracked file in the stash's third parent. So in a workspace with lots of untracked files, every one of them was a candidate path and cost two git processes (the first lookup always misses for untracked files). The reporter's case is a Rust `target/` directory that isn't gitignored. Each task completion spawned thousands of git processes at once, which is the flood of `git show ...:target/debug/.fingerprint/...` processes and zombies in the issue.

The fix looks up checkpoint blobs in bulk and reads them in one batch:
- `git diff --raw -z --no-abbrev --no-renames <ref>` gives the checkpoint blob for each changed tracked path, so lookups scale with the number of changes rather than the repo size.
- `git ls-tree -r -z <ref>^3` gives the blobs for files that were untracked at snapshot time. main already listed this tree.
- `git cat-file --batch-check` gets blob sizes, and `git cat-file --batch` reads every needed blob in one process.

A comparison now always runs 6 git processes, no matter how many files there are. Behavior is otherwise unchanged:
- The checkpoint's own tree is checked first, then the third parent.
- Files missing from the checkpoint compare as `""`.
- Blobs larger than the old 50 MB `maxBuffer` limit are still treated as `""`.

### Test Procedure

- **Automated:** checkpoint diff, restore, and hook tests pass, plus the full `@cline/core` unit suite (3,115 tests). Typecheck passes and Biome is clean. I added a test for nested paths that contain spaces.
- **Edge cases, old vs new output byte-identical:** files untracked after the checkpoint (both edited and unchanged), binary content, a symlink retarget, and a newly staged file.
- **CLI smoke test:**
  - Ran real agent turns in a repo with 3,000 untracked `target/` files that aren't gitignored, plus a pre-existing untracked `notes.txt`.
  - Each turn created a stash checkpoint.
  - Comparing against those checkpoints gave byte-identical results with main, using 12 git processes instead of 12,017.
  - `/undo` with "Restore chat and workspace" restored `main.rs`, removed the agent-created file, brought `notes.txt` back, and left `target/` untouched.
- **VS Code extension smoke test:**
  - Same workspace, in the Extension Development Host with real tasks.
  - "View Changes" showed the correct diffs after each turn, with no `target/` files.
  - "Reset Code" on a message ran the real restore (`reset --hard`, `clean -fd`, `stash apply`) and re-ran the message.
  - A monitor sampled processes every 0.25 s for 89 minutes. Git never had more than 3 processes running at once. A git zombie appeared in only 6 of about 19,600 samples, one at a time, which is the normal gap before Node reaps a finished child. Memory went back down after each comparison.

title: fix(core): don't start a second runtime for a session whose turn is running
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (found while diagnosing a desktop "stall" from a diagnostics export)

### Description

If a session was started by id while its turn was still running, `LocalRuntimeHost.startSession` built a new runtime and replaced the live entry in `this.sessions`. The old agent wasn't stopped. It kept running, and nothing could reach it any more:

- Stop aborted only the new runtime.
- The hidden turn kept calling tools (auto-approved, if that's on). None of its work reached the transcript, and the UI showed the chat as stopped.
- Its final reply was never shown.

The desktop triggers this every time you send a follow-up mid-turn to a chat reopened from the sidebar. Reopening sets `hydratedHistorySessionId`, and the next send then calls `start` with the existing id before `send` (`webview/hooks/use-chat-session.ts`, the `hydratedHistorySessionId === activeSessionId` branch). The hub passes that straight to the host.

**Fix:** when `startSession` gets the id of a live session whose agent is busy (`!agent.canStartRun()`), it returns that session instead of building a new one. The client's next `send` then queues behind the running turn, like any prompt sent mid-turn, and Stop reaches the one real agent. A start that also carries a prompt for a busy session now throws instead of silently creating a duplicate. The fix is in the host rather than the desktop, so every caller is covered.

Out of scope: restarting an **idle** live session still replaces its runtime without shutting the old one down. That can't cause a hidden running turn, so it's left for a separate change.

#### Evidence from the original report
From a desktop 0.0.48 diagnostics export (chat `1792515462297_5soNH`):
- `20:57:28` `session.create` for the chat while `run.start` `hubreq_…ldfzo` (started 20:25) was still pending.
- `20:57:29.813` and `.847`: two `hook.beforeModel` 34 ms apart, meaning two agents on one chat.
- `21:00:58` `run.abort` stopped only the new run. The hub log then shows a tool call roughly every 30 s for that chat until `21:08:56`, and none of them are in the transcript.
- `21:08:30` the user typed "resume" to get the chat moving again.

### Repro steps (desktop, before this fix)

1. In Cline desktop, open any repo and start a chat with auto-approve on. Send: `Use the shell tool to run "sleep 30" four times, one call at a time, and after each one say "done N".`
2. While the first `sleep 30` is running, click a different chat in the sidebar, then click back to the first chat.
3. Send a follow-up while it's still working, for example `also, what's 2+2?`
4. Press **Stop**.

**Expected:** all work stops.

**Actual (bug):**
- The chat shows as stopped, but `pgrep -fl "sleep 30"` keeps finding a new `sleep 30` about every 30 s.
- `~/.cline/data/logs/hub-daemon.log` keeps logging `hook.beforeTool` and `hook.beforeModel` for the chat's session id after the `run.abort` line.
- Before the Stop, the same log shows a `session.create` for that id while its earlier `run.start` hasn't logged `command.end`, followed by two `hook.beforeModel` entries milliseconds apart.

**With this fix:** the follow-up is queued and the counting run keeps going in the visible chat. Stop ends everything, and `pgrep` finds no new `sleep` processes.

### Test Procedure

- New unit test `reuses a session whose turn is running instead of starting a second runtime under its id` (`local-runtime-host.test.ts`). It starts a slow turn, starts the same id again with persisted messages as the desktop does, and checks two things: no second agent is built, and `abort` settles the original turn as `aborted`.
    - It fails without the fix (`createAgent` called 2 times).
- `bunx vitest run src/runtime/host/`: 145 passed. `bun run typecheck` in `@cline/core` passes. Biome is clean.
- `src/hub/server`: 21 of 22 files pass. The one failing file, `ui-events.test.ts`, fails with `HubLockHeldError` because a real hub was running on the test machine. It isn't related to this change.
