**Issue:** N/A. Follow-up to #15278 (Tauri CLI 2.11.4 to 2.12.3), found while reviewing that bump. It should merge before the next desktop release from `main`.

### Description

**Problem.** #15278 moved the Tauri CLI to 2.12.3, but the Rust crates stayed on the 2.11 line (`tauri` 2.11.1, `tauri-build` 2.6.1). That mismatch breaks Windows:

- CLI 2.11.x and earlier set `STATIC_VCRUNTIME=true` for every `cargo build`. `tauri-build` 2.6.1 links the MSVC runtime statically only when that variable is `"true"`.
- CLI 2.12.0 stopped setting it (tauri-apps/tauri#15401). It expects `tauri-build` >= 2.7, which reads `build.windows.staticVCRuntime` instead (default `true`).

On current `main`, `cline-app.exe` therefore imports `VCRUNTIME140.dll` and `VCRUNTIME140_1.dll`. On machines without the VC++ redistributable, the app fails to launch, and that includes existing users who auto-update. GitHub's Windows runners have the redistributable installed, so CI and the smoke tests don't notice.

**Fix.** Upgrade the Rust runtime and the JS API to the 2.12 line that matches the CLI. Every version picked has at least a week of soak:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tauri` | 2.11.1 | 2.12.4 |
| `tauri-build` / `-codegen` / `-macros` | 2.6.1 | 2.7.3 |
| `tauri-runtime` / `-runtime-wry` | 2.11.1 | 2.12.2 |
| `tauri-utils` | 2.9.1 | 2.10.2 |
| `wry` / `tao` | 0.55.1 / 0.35.2 | 0.57.0 / 0.37.1 |
| `@tauri-apps/api` | 2.11.1 | 2.12.4 |

The rest of the `Cargo.lock` diff is what `tauri` 2.12.4 requires (`tray-icon` 0.25, `muda` 0.20, `windows` 0.62, `webview2-com` 0.39, ...). Nothing in it was published after Oct 15. The `Cargo.toml` floors (`tauri` 2.12.4, `tauri-build` 2.7.3) keep the lock from resolving back to an older `tauri-build`. The 2.7.3 floor also skips 2.7.0-2.7.2, which had a stub `msvcrt.lib` linking bug (tauri-apps/tauri#16238). Plugins (updater, notification, single-instance) are unchanged, so their Rust and JS versions still match. In `bun.lock` I reverted the unrelated `zod` re-nesting by hand, so the diff is only the `@tauri-apps/api` entry.

**Runtime changes reviewed (2.11.1 to 2.12.4, wry 0.57, tao 0.37):** mostly bug fixes plus new APIs we don't use. The ones that touch our app:

- **macOS `restart()`** (used by update-apply and relaunch) now relaunches through LaunchServices (`open -n`) instead of spawning the binary directly. The new process no longer inherits the old stdio or process group. Ordering and the single-instance cleanup are unchanged.
- **Windows undecorated-window fixes** (our Windows window is undecorated): no title-bar flash on creation and fewer visibility flickers. tao also exits cleanly on `WM_ENDSESSION`. Previously that crashed when Restart Manager, which our NSIS hook uses, closed the app.
- **macOS traffic-light inset** is re-applied after title changes and fullscreen (we use `titleBarStyle: Overlay`).
- **Linux Wayland decoration handling** changed (server-side vs. client-side decorations).
- **Event-listener and channel leak fixes**, and an IPC security fix (GHSA-w28w-mhc8-qvjv).
- **Windows 7 support dropped.** WebView2 already doesn't support Windows 7.

### Test Procedure

- **Windows static linking:** cross-compiled `cline-app.exe` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with `cargo xwin`, with no `STATIC_VCRUNTIME` set, and checked its imports.
  - Shipped v0.0.48: no VC runtime imports.
  - `main` (CLI 2.12.3 + `tauri-build` 2.6.1): imports `VCRUNTIME140.dll` and `VCRUNTIME140_1.dll`.
  - This PR: no VC runtime imports.
- **Linux prod build** (`tauri build --bundles deb,rpm --config src-tauri/tauri.release.conf.json`, after merging the latest `main`):
  - The CLI version-mismatch check passes, and the RPM step takes ~11s.
  - Both updater signatures verify with the code the updater in current prod builds uses (`tauri-plugin-updater` 2.10.1 / `minisign-verify` 0.2.5).
- **Installed .deb smoke test:**
  - The app launches, onboarding advances, and the main UI renders.
  - The webview re-lays out when the window is resized.
  - Closing the window hides it to the tray, and the backend and Hub start.
- **macOS:** the AppKit/`objc2` crates are unchanged (0.6.4 / 0.3.2). The macOS-only Tauri APIs we call (`RunEvent::Reopen`, `icon_as_template`, `run_on_main_thread`, `set_fullscreen`, `set_text`) have unchanged signatures. I couldn't compile for macOS here (`ring` needs the macOS SDK), so the nightly is the macOS compile gate.
- `bun run typecheck`, the desktop webview tests that use `@tauri-apps/api` (50 pass), and `scripts/windows-installer.test.ts` + `scripts/generate-update-manifest.test.ts` pass.
- **After merge:** run a nightly on all four targets.
  - Check `dumpbin /dependents cline-app.exe` lists no `VCRUNTIME140.dll`.
  - On a Windows machine, install the nightly over v0.0.48.
  - On macOS, check the app relaunches after "Restart to update".

## Summary

The CLI parsed integer flags with `Number.parseInt`, so values such as `10m`, `1.5`, and `1e3` were accepted by their numeric prefix. The validation now covers root `--timeout` and `--retries`, history `--limit`, and schedule timeout, max-parallel, and limit options. Invalid schedule values are rejected before any hub command is sent.

title: fix(desktop): skip routine hub polling in diagnostics exports
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (found while reading stall reports from teammates)

### Description

**The problem**

When someone sends us a diagnostics report for a stuck task, the hub log section often doesn't reach back far enough to show what happened.

The report keeps only the last 2 MB of the hub log. An open Desktop app checks in with the hub every few seconds to refresh its task list and schedules, and each check-in writes two log lines. On an idle machine, that routine chatter fills the whole 2 MB in about half a day. In one recent report the hub section covered 11.6 hours, nearly all of it these check-ins, and the runs we needed to see had already been cut off.

**The fix**

The report now looks further back through the hub log (the last 32 MB instead of 2 MB). It leaves out the routine check-ins, then keeps the same 2 MB, so reports are no bigger than before.

- Only completed, successful check-ins are dropped: `session.list`, `settings.list` and `schedule.*`. A check-in that failed keeps both its lines, a check-in that never finished keeps its start line, and every other line is untouched.
- The section title now says "routine polling omitted", so whoever reads the report knows lines were left out.
- The Desktop app's own log section is unchanged.

**How much further back it reaches**

| Hub log | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| The idle machine from the report above | ~11.6 hours | up to ~8 days (about 16× more of the raw log) |
| A busy local hub log | 14 days | 29 days |

title: fix(cli): list openai-compatible models when the key is in OPENAI_API_KEY
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15284

### Description

With an `openai-compatible` provider, the `/model` picker lists no models when the API key is supplied via the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable instead of being stored in `providers.json`. It works when the key is in `providers.json`.

Cause: the model list is fetched with `GET <baseUrl>/models`, and the key for that request was read only from `config.apiKey` (the stored value). When the key lives only in `OPENAI_API_KEY`, the request went out with no `Authorization` header, so the provider returned nothing and the picker showed an empty list. The agent request path already resolves the key from the provider's declared `apiKeyEnv` (`OPENAI_API_KEY` for `openai-compatible`), which is why chatting worked while model listing did not.

Fix: fall back to `OPENAI_API_KEY` when no key is stored, matching the request path's resolution order (stored key first, then env). The fallback is gated on `providerId === "openai-compatible"` so the OpenAI key is never sent to an unrelated provider. The helper was extracted into its own module so it can be unit tested without the TUI hook (verbatim move, no behavior change beyond the fallback).

### Test Procedure

- Added `openai-compatible-models.test.ts` with three cases: the env-key fallback sends `Authorization: Bearer <OPENAI_API_KEY>`; a non-openai-compatible provider does not receive the env key; a stored `apiKey` takes precedence over the env var.
- Verified red before / green after: with the fallback removed the env-key test fails (no auth header); with the fix all three pass.
- Ran the related model-selector suites (19 tests) plus package typecheck and lint: all clean.

title: chore: make @saoudrizwan sole code owner of .github/ and README.md
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (repo governance change)

### Description

Makes @saoudrizwan the only code owner for `/.github/` and `/README.md`.

**Why:** The `Main branch protection` ruleset (applies to `main` and `legacy-extension`) already has `require_code_owner_review: true`. But CODEOWNERS listed several owners per path, and GitHub accepts an approval from **any one** of them. So changes to workflows, composite actions, and CODEOWNERS itself could merge without Saoud seeing them. Workflow files control publish pipelines, secrets, and environment gates (PublishNPM, PublishDesktop, etc.), so we want a single reviewer on that surface.

Before:
```
/.github/   @saoudrizwan @arafatkatze @maxpaulus43 @dominiccooney
/README.md  @saoudrizwan @juanpflores
```
After:
```
/.github/   @saoudrizwan
/README.md  @saoudrizwan
```

**Gotchas / what this does NOT cover:**
- The ruleset lets `OrganizationAdmin` bypass it (`bypass_mode: always`), so org admins can still merge without code-owner review. Closing that gap means removing the bypass actor in repo settings. That's a settings change, not something this PR can do.
- The `Desktop Experimental` ruleset is separate and may not require code-owner review.
- `/.github/` covers `.github/CODEOWNERS`, so later changes to ownership also need Saoud's approval.

title: build(desktop): bump @tauri-apps/cli to 2.12.3 for fast RPM bundling
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A. Found while watching a desktop nightly (run [38838870590](https://github.com/cline/cline/actions/runs/38838870590)) take ~26 min on Linux.

### Description

**Problem.** The Linux desktop build jobs are by far the slowest jobs in `desktop-publish.yml` (Linux x64 ~26 min, arm64 ~30 min, vs. macOS/Windows ~13 min), and they keep getting slower. Almost all of that time is spent in one place: Tauri writing the `.rpm`.

From the x64 job log of the nightly above:

```
02:15:37  Bundling Cline Nightly_..._amd64.deb
02:15:45  Bundling Cline Nightly-...x86_64.rpm      <- deb took 8s
02:35:07  Finished 2 bundles                        <- rpm took 19.5 min
```

Over time the RPM step went 5.5 min (Oct 2) → 11 min (Oct 14) → 19.5 min (Oct 16) → 18.4 min (Oct 17), while the payload only grew ~1.5× (the bundled Bun-compiled CLI is ~130 MB, x3 copies with the remote helper/backend; ~442 MB uncompressed, 168 files).

**Root cause.** `@tauri-apps/cli` 2.11.4 (what `bun.lock` pinned) bundles `tauri-bundler` with **`rpm` crate 0.16.0**. Its compressed-payload path is pathologically slow on large payloads, regardless of algorithm or level. Every released CLI up to and including 2.12.2 still ships `rpm` 0.16.0; **2.12.3 is the first that ships `rpm` 0.30.2**.

**Fix.** Bump `@tauri-apps/cli` to `^2.12.3` (lockfile resolves 2.12.3). The floor in `package.json` is raised from `^2.0.0` so nobody can resolve back onto a slow CLI. Rust crates (`tauri` 2.11.1 etc.) are untouched; `Cargo.lock` doesn't change. The CLI only drives the build/bundle.

### How I verified the root cause

I downloaded the nightly's `.deb`, extracted its payload (exactly the files that go into the RPM), and wrote a tiny Rust harness that feeds those files into `rpm::PackageBuilder` the same way `tauri-bundler`'s `rpm.rs` does. Timings in the dev container:

| `rpm` crate | Compression | Time | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.16.0 (CLI ≤ 2.12.2) | gzip 6 (Tauri default) | **395 s** | 163 MB |
| 0.16.0 | gzip 1 | 503 s | 189 MB |
| 0.16.0 | zstd 3 | 331 s | 156 MB |
| 0.16.0 | none | 2.8 s | 442 MB |
| **0.30.2 (CLI 2.12.3)** | gzip 6 | **7.6 s** | 163 MB |

For scale, `tar | gzip -6` over the same tree takes ~9.7 s. CI runners are ~3× slower than the container, which matches the ~19 min seen in Actions.

### Alternatives considered

- **Setting `bundle.linux.rpm.compression`** (the obvious one-line fix): doesn't help. Lower gzip levels and zstd are all still 5+ min on the old crate. Only `none` is fast, and that ships a ~440 MB RPM (2.7× bigger downloads).
- **Dropping the RPM on the nightly channel**: hides the problem only for nightlies; stable/beta stay slow.
- **2.12.4** (latest): released Oct 21; my bun config's 7-day `minimumReleaseAge` held it back. 2.12.3 has the same `rpm` 0.30.2 and a week of soak, so I went with it.

### Gotcha: lockfile churn

A plain `bun update @tauri-apps/cli` (or any lockfile re-save) also re-hoists the root `zod` from 4.4.3 → 4.6.5 (currently nested under `@jerome-benoit/sap-ai-provider`). That's unrelated, so I reverted those lines by hand; the diff is only the `@tauri-apps/cli*` entries. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes.

### Test Procedure

- `bunx tauri --version` → `tauri-cli 2.12.3`; `bunx tauri info` resolves fine against `tauri` 2.11.1.
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes.
- The real verification is a desktop nightly from `main` after merge. The CLI drives macOS (universal lipo + signing + notarization), Windows (NSIS + `signCommand`) and Linux bundling, so all four build jobs plus the smoke tests need to go green, and Linux x64's "Build desktop bundles" step should drop from ~24 min to ~5 min. I'll run one right after merge, before the next stable.

title: fix(llms): explain provider timeouts in plain words and record where they happened
body:
## What was wrong

When a model provider accepts a request and then sends nothing, the run sits for 5 minutes until Bun's built-in fetch timeout gives up. The user then sees only "The operation timed out.", which doesn't say what happened or what to do. Telemetry records the same raw text, so there is no easy way to tell a provider that never started replying from one that stopped partway through.

In the last 7 days, the CLI and Desktop logged about 4,400 of these timeouts, almost all on cheap or free models.

## What this changes

- **Plain message.** When a timeout ends the run, the user sees either "The model provider stopped responding before it started its reply." or "The model provider stopped responding partway through its reply.", followed by "Send a message to continue, or switch models if this keeps happening."
- **Telemetry.** `sdk.error` gets a `timeoutPhase` field (`before_reply` or `mid_reply`), so a model or provider that starts going silent can be spotted and alerted on. The raw error text in telemetry is unchanged.

Retry decisions and time limits are unchanged: a timeout still ends the run after the same wait.

## How it was tested

- New gateway tests make the stream throw Bun's `TimeoutError`, once before any content and once after some text. They check the message the user sees, the raw error text and `timeoutPhase` in `sdk.error`, and that the error is still not retried.
- An end-to-end run through a real hub against a fake provider that goes silent, before replying and partway through, shows the new messages after the usual 300-second wait. Normal replies and dropped connections behave as before.

title: fix: stop serializing desktop session transcript twice into session.create
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15203

### Description

Desktop sessions serialize the full chat transcript twice into a single `session.create` frame, so any session larger than the hub's websocket frame limit (around 8 MiB) fails to resume with `1006 (Received too big message)`.

Root cause: `initialMessages` is a top-level field of `StartSessionInput` and `manager.start()` reads it from there. But `buildCoreSessionConfig` also set `initialMessages` on the core session config, and `splitCoreSessionConfig` spreads every non-local-runtime key into the transport `config`. So the transcript rode inside `config` **and** again at the top level, duplicating it in one frame. The desktop start path also re-embedded it a second time.

Nothing reads `initialMessages` from the transport config (every consumer reads the top-level `input.initialMessages` / `payload.initialMessages`), so the embedded copy was pure overhead that doubled the frame size.

Fix: remove the embed from `buildCoreSessionConfig` and the redundant copy in the start path. All three start paths (start, resume, fork) already pass `initialMessages` top-level, so the transcript still reaches the runtime exactly once.

### Test Procedure

- Added a regression test in `apps/examples/desktop-app/sidecar/chat-session.test.ts` asserting that the start input carries `initialMessages` at the top level and **not** inside `.config`. It fails on the current code (the transcript is duplicated inside `config`) and passes with this change.
- Ran the full `chat-session.test.ts` suite: 101/101 pass.
- Verified the resume and fork paths still deliver the transcript, since each already passes `initialMessages` top-level to `manager.start`.
- Change is a removal with no new types, so the transport contract is unchanged (the key was an untyped extra).

title: ci: require PublishNPM approval for every npm publish
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A (release hardening)

### Description

Every npm publish (the `cline` CLI, its six `@cline/cli-*` platform packages, the SDK packages, and `@cline/ui`) now needs a person to approve the run before anything ships. The desktop app and the VS Code extension already work this way.

**What changes**

- `cli-publish.yml`, `sdk-publish.yml`, and `ui-publish.yml` publish jobs now run in the new **`PublishNPM`** GitHub environment (required reviewer, deployment branches limited to `main`). Runs pause in `waiting` until someone clicks "Review deployments". That's expected, not a hang.
- **Nightly crons removed, nightlies kept.** The CLI (`0 12 * * *`) and SDK (`0 2 * * *`) crons are gone. An approval-gated cron would sit `waiting` every day. The extension's `PublishNightly` gate showed this: nobody approves it, so it never ships. Both nightlies still exist as manual dispatches (`cli-publish -f publish_target=nightly`, `sdk-publish -f channel=nightly`), and they're gated like every other publish.
- `@cline/ui` gets the gate back. #12938 removed it to avoid a two-person approval step. `PublishNPM` currently has a single reviewer, so this is one click.
- Docs and skills (`publish-cli`, `publish-ui`, `DISTRIBUTION.md`, `sdk/CONTRIBUTING.md`) say nightlies are manual-only and mention the approval step.

**Why the workflow change alone isn't enough**

The `environment:` line is only half of it. A copy of a workflow run from another branch could leave the line out. The enforcement comes from the npm side: each package's trusted-publisher entry gets `environment = PublishNPM`, so npm rejects OIDC tokens from any job that wasn't approved in that environment. That's a settings change on npmjs.com, done after this merges.

### Rollout order (matters)

1. **Merge this PR.** Publishes keep working; they just pause for approval.
2. **Azure:** CLI Windows signing authenticates over OIDC. Once the job runs in an environment, the token subject changes from `repo:cline/cline:ref:refs/heads/main` to `repo:cline/cline:environment:PublishNPM`. Add a federated credential with that subject to the Entra app used for CLI signing **before the next CLI release**, or signing fails.
3. **npm:** for each package, set the trusted publisher's environment to `PublishNPM` and confirm "Require two-factor authentication and disallow tokens". Doing this before step 1 would break every publish.

### Gotchas

- The `nightly` dist-tag now only moves when someone dispatches and approves a nightly, so `cline@nightly` users get updates less often.
- The SDK `test` job still runs before approval, so you approve a run that has already gone green.
- The `publish-cli` skill still has a local publish path (`bun release cli`). With tokens disallowed, that only works for a maintainer publishing interactively with 2FA.

### Test Procedure

- Parsed all three workflows with `Bun.YAML.parse`.
- Checked the `PublishNPM` environment via the API: required reviewer set, branch policy `main`.
- The real end-to-end check is the next CLI release. It should pause for approval, sign the Windows binaries (after the Azure step), and publish with provenance.

title: fix(core): stop re-cutting read_files results to the 8k tool-result cap
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** Fixes #13923 · [CLINE-3196](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3196)

Related: #13263 (the `read_files` half of it), #14257 (closed in favour of this change).

### Description

A file read passes through two caps that were set independently and never matched up:

- `read_files` bounds its own output at 2000 lines / ~48k characters and tells the model so, both in the tool description and in a per-read footer (`[Showing lines 1-424 of 1500. Use start_line/end_line to read other sections.]`).
- `MessageBuilder` then cuts **every** tool result to 8k characters on the way to the provider, middle-out, with a bare `...[truncated N chars]...` marker.

So a read the model was just told it received in full reaches it ~17% intact. Ranged reads that fit the tool cap carry no footer at all, so there the cut is the only signal — a 345-line range comes back as its first and last ~60 lines. Models respond by paging in ever smaller slices, concluding the tool is broken, and falling back to `cat`/`sed` through the shell (see the issue and the Discord report that prompted this).

The 8k tool-result cap was introduced for command and MCP output, where it was measured; file reads already had a purpose-built cap with paging guidance. `MessageBuilder` also already has a looser 50k cap for file content — user `file` attachments were routed to it precisely so the aggressive tool-result cap would not mutilate them. This change routes read-tool results to that same cap. A well-formed read (≤ ~48.1k with line-number prefixes and footer) is now never re-cut; the 50k cap remains a backstop for a custom read executor that ignores the tool's bounds. Nothing else moves: `run_commands`, search, MCP and custom tools keep the 8k cap; the aggregate 6MB request budget and the stale-read rewrite still bound history growth.

A `maxToolResultChars` that is configured explicitly (option or `CLINE_MESSAGE_BUILDER_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS`) keeps its documented meaning of capping every tool result, so it also bounds reads: the read cap is `min(50k, explicit cap)`, and the 50k default only applies when no override is set.

Two existing tests encoded the 8k cut on read fixtures and were adjusted to keep their intent (image siblings preserved while text truncates; stale-read batching counts provider-bound bytes, not raw history bytes) under the read cap.

### Test Procedure

- New unit tests in `message-builder.test.ts` ("read-result cap"): a tool-capped 48k `read_files` window is sent whole (structured and string content), a 60k read result is still cut at the file-content cap, `run_commands` output is still cut at 8k, and an explicit `maxToolResultChars` — as an option and via the env var — still bounds reads while an empty environment keeps the 50k default. The first two fail on `main`.
- New `message-builder.read-files.test.ts` drives the real `read_files` tool through `MessageBuilder` with a 751-line markdown file — whole file, lines 55-400 and lines 110-230, i.e. the reads from the report — plus a batched two-file read, and asserts what the tool returned is what the provider request carries. The single-file cases fail on `main` (7,967 / 7,895 / 7,955 chars of 47,384 / 23,648 / 8,280 reach the model).
- `@cline/core` unit suite, `tsc` and Biome green.

Workaround for affected users until this ships: `CLINE_MESSAGE_BUILDER_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS=50000` in the environment the IDE/CLI starts from (raises the cap for every tool, not only reads).

-   [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

title: feat(core): import Cursor sessions into Cline Desktop
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** https://github.com/cline/cline/discussions/15252

### Description

Cline Desktop can import past sessions from Claude Code, Codex and opencode. This adds Cursor.

The new `cursor` adapter in `@cline/core` reads Cursor's local chat store (`User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`). It lists each conversation once, using Cursor's composer id as the source id, so the existing dedup works. Tool calls keep their ids and results, and timestamps, model, workspace folder and git branch carry over. Drafts, subagents, empty conversations and Claude Code mirrors are skipped.

The database is only ever opened read-only. When Cursor is closed it uses an immutable open, so no side files are created. While Cursor is running it acts as a normal read-only reader of the live WAL, and only when Cursor's own `-wal` and `-shm` already exist. In any other state it fails with a clear message rather than risk creating files. Reads go through a fixed list of JSON fields, so Cursor's stored secrets and encryption keys are never read. Malformed rows are skipped instead of hiding every session.

Cursor is also listed in the desktop import dialog, Settings → Import and the docs.

Credit to @treeuri: #13910 explored Cursor's agent-transcript files. Those transcripts have no tool ids, results or timestamps, so this PR reads the store instead. A transcript fallback for sessions that aren't in the store is a planned follow-up.

### Test Procedure

- `vitest src/services/session-import`: 55 tests. They use synthetic stores and cover:
  - the live-WAL reader and the no-WAL immutable path, including a Bun subprocess run
  - no side files on a corrupt store or a `-wal` without `-shm`
  - write rejection, and the source file staying byte-identical
  - planted fake secrets never being read
  - malformed rows, filters, mapping, turn boundaries, per-turn models and safe truncation
  - the cwd chain and service dedup
- Desktop: session-import, import-view and sessions-view tests (27). `@cline/core` typechecks at every commit; `@cline/code` at HEAD.
- Real Cursor 3.22 store (counts only, nothing imported): 123 sessions discovered, 123 converted with 0 errors. Discovery takes about 90 ms and the slowest conversion 33 ms. Cursor's database hash, mtime and folder listing were unchanged afterwards.
- Desktop dev app with a synthetic Cursor home: Cursor shows in Settings → Import and in the dialog, and an imported session opens with the "Imported from Cursor" notice.

### Type of Change

Some tests fail on main@0870796 as well, so the second box is unchecked. Four `@cline/core` hub-server tests fail on both. The desktop `test:sidecar` and `test:settings-ui` suites fail identically on Node 26 because of its built-in `localStorage`; with `--no-experimental-webstorage` they pass except one worktree test that also fails on main. Touched files pass Biome.

**Privacy:** nothing is written to Cursor's directories. Errors and logs never include message text, titles or paths. Test fixtures are synthetic.

title: feat: show ChatGPT subscription usage windows in VS Code
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** https://github.com/cline/cline/discussions/15251

### Description

When Cline runs on a ChatGPT subscription, task cost is hidden (#13552), and users only find out they're near their rolling limits when a request fails. This shows the usage the provider reports, with percent used and reset time per window, in the VS Code task header and in the ChatGPT Subscription provider settings. Each report shows how old it is, and stale or unknown values are labelled.

On `finish-step`, the direct `openai-codex` provider reads exactly six response headers: `x-codex-{primary,secondary}-{used-percent,window-minutes,reset-at}`. Capture is passive, with no new requests or polling. Malformed data is ignored, and accounting, retries and error handling are unchanged. The snapshot travels through a dedicated SDK event that stays out of chunks, telemetry, persistence, hub projection and CLI JSON. It is documented in `sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

### Test Procedure

- New parser and gateway tests cover complete, partial, missing and malformed headers, values over 100%, and exclusion of unrelated or credential headers.
- Runtime, Core, VS Code state and privacy tests cover event pass-through, exclusions, session/provider/credential invalidation and stale-packet ordering. UI tests cover normal, near/at limit, stale, unknown or passed reset, and no data.
- SDK build and unit suites, workspace types, extension/webview builds and unit suites, and lint on touched files all pass. Each commit typechecks on its own.
- Core: 4 hub-server tests in `src/hub/server/index.test.ts` fail identically on main@0870796. A fifth (`falls back to an ephemeral port when fallback is allowed`) is flaky on both trees, failing once in 3 alternating runs on each. The plugin-registry timeout test also fails on main. This PR doesn't touch hub or plugin code.
- Still to do: a manual check in a signed-in extension host. Opened as a draft until then.

### Type of Change

-   [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [ ] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`): see the pre-existing Core failures above
-   [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Screenshots

All values are synthetic. Each image shows the real `TaskHeader` (left) and the ChatGPT Subscription provider settings card (right).

**Normal**
![Normal usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/victory-c/cline/pr-screenshots/subscription-usage/ui-normal.jpg)

**Near and at the limit** (warning at 80% or more, error at 100%)
![Near limit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/victory-c/cline/pr-screenshots/subscription-usage/ui-near.jpg)

![Stale report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/victory-c/cline/pr-screenshots/subscription-usage/ui-stale.jpg)

![No data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/victory-c/cline/pr-screenshots/subscription-usage/ui-no-data.jpg)

### Additional Notes

**Privacy:** only the six numeric fields enter an in-memory snapshot. Credentials, account identity and raw headers are never copied. Usage reports stay out of logs, telemetry, transcripts, task history, generic output, CLI JSON and hub persistence. Fixtures and screenshots are synthetic.

**Known gaps:** Codex CLI, Claude Code, desktop and CLI UI are deferred. Only the default Codex pool and the primary agent are covered. Credential changes made in another VS Code window aren't detected. Nothing is captured from 429 responses. Reloading clears the snapshot until the next response.
